key_insight: A kernel-method analysis links random feature and collocation budgets to convergence bounds for solving linear PDEs.
engineering_relevance: The theory helps characterize how feature count, collocation count, and activation smoothness constrain PDE solution accuracy.
method: Analyze finite random-feature approximation in Sobolev norms and the PDE residual seminorm.
Relate approximation and noiseless RKHS collocation estimation to kernel ridge regression.
Derive eigenvalue-based upper and lower bounds, including a joint resource lower bound.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds rather than numerical benchmarks, with algebraic eigenvalue upper bounds for finitely smooth activations and stretched-exponential bounds for analytic activations.
watch_item: The estimation analysis assumes noiseless collocation observations; applicability to noisy data requires separate justification.
paper_title: A Convergence Analysis of the Random Feature Method for Linear PDEs
